summary: Bryan W. Van Norden is a scholar of philosophy and sinology who studied at Stanford University from ~1985 to 1991. Around 1996, he became a professor at Vassar College in Philosophy and Chinese & Japanese.
Bryce Ryan was an indologist who held academic posts at Cornell University and the University of Ceylon, where he taught Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah.

Bulcsu Siklós is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his PhD from the University of London under supervisor Tadeusz Skorupski and teacher Charles R. Bawden. He was affiliated with SOAS University of London in 1996.

Bunga Fukui (1934–2017) worked in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Demiéville, Maxime Kaltenmark, and Rolf A. Stein, later serving as professor at Waseda (~1978–2004).

Bunkyo Aoki (1886–1956) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University under Kōzui Ōtani and became a lecturer in Tibetan at the University of Tokyo in 1951, succeeding Tokan Tada.

Bunsaku Kurata (1918–1983) studied at Aoyama Gakuin and Waseda University. Active in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology, he served at the Tokyo National Museum, the National Commission for Protection of Cultural Properties, and became Director of Nara National Museum in 1975.

Bunyiu Nanjio (1849–1927) was an indologist, sinologist, and Buddhist scholar. He studied at Otani University and Oxford under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell, later serving as a lecturer at Tokyo University and long-term director at Otani University.

Bunzaburo Matsumoto (1869–1944) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, indology, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Rikkyo University, First Higher School, and Kyoto University (1906–1929), later directing its Institute for Research in Humanities.

Burchard Brentjes (1929–2012) worked in archaeology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1947–1952) under Heinz Mode, served on its faculty from ~1954 to 1974, and succeeded Mode in 1978.

Burkhard Quessel is a scholar of Tibetology and indology who studied at the University of Hamburg, where he was a member in 1997. Between 2002 and 2012, he was attested as a curator at the British Library.
Burton Stein (1926–1996) was a historian and indologist. He served on the faculties of the University of Hawaiʻi from ~1968 to 1988 and SOAS University of London from ~1988 to 1996.

Burton Watson (1925–2017) worked in sinology, japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University and Columbia University under L. Carrington Goodrich, Chi-chen Wang, and Wm. Theodore de Bary, later holding posts at Columbia and Stanford University.

C. D. Sebastian is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and indology who earned his PhD from Banaras Hindu University. Having studied with Paul Williams, Gavin D'Costa, and Ashok Kumar Chatterjee, he became Professor of Indian Philosophy at IIT Bombay (attested 2016).
C. Kunhan Raja (1895–1963) was an indologist who served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras, attested in 1927 and 1946.
C. R. Krishnamacharlu (b. 1888) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and indology who completed his studies at Madras Christian College and Pachaiyappa's College.
C. S. Srinivasachari (1890–1951) was an indologist and historian who held professorships at Pachaiyappa's College and Annamalai University (attested 1932–1933).
C. S. Sundaram was an indologist who held posts at Madras Sanskrit College and the University of Madras, where he was appointed Reader in Sanskrit in 1951.

C. W. Huntington, Jr. (1949–2020) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1980–1986) under Luis O. Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, later serving as professor at Hartwick College (~2000–2020).

Calambur Sivaramamurti (1910–1983) was an indologist and archaeologist who studied at Presidency College, Chennai under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He held curatorial posts at the Government Museum Chennai, Indian Museum, Archaeological Survey of India, and the National Museum, New Delhi.

Calvert Watkins (1933–2013) was a linguist and indologist who studied at Harvard University, EPHE, and DIAS. He served as professor of linguistics and classics at Harvard (1959–2003) and subsequently as distinguished professor at UCLA (2003–2013).
